title_en: Bank of China, Beijing Branch v. Lida Aquarium — dispute over letter of credit advance
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where there is no genuine trade background between the parties, but they apply to a bank for issuance of a letter of credit in the name of importing goods, resulting in a large outflow of bank funds and harming state interests, the relationship of applying for the letter of credit shall be held invalid, and the guarantee provided by the guarantor for such purpose shall also be invalid.

full_text_en:
Bank of China Beijing Branch v. Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Letter of Credit Advance Payment

【Ruling Summary】

I. Where the parties involved have no genuine trade background but apply to a bank for the issuance of letters of credit under the guise of importing goods, thereby causing a significant outflow of bank funds and harming national interests, the application for the letter of credit relationship shall be held invalid, and any guarantee provided by a guarantor in connection therewith shall likewise be invalid.

II. Although the parties have explicitly chosen relevant international practices as the basis for their principal-agent relationship concerning the issuance of letters of credit, such practices are inapplicable to the legal relationship of principal-agent for the issuance of letters of credit between the issuing bank and the applicant. The matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of domestic law.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 15

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Bank of China Beijing Branch, domiciled at Asia Pacific Building, No. 8 Yabao Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Person in Charge: Xie Zhiyong, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Yu Fan, Head of Asset Preservation Division of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Huaizhou, Staff of Asset Preservation Division of the Branch.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 137 Xizhimenwai Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Zong Ying, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Han Jiayi, Lawyer of Beijing Jingdu Law Firm, Shanghai Branch.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yingzi, Legal Counsel of the Company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at Block C, No. 5 Anding Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Liu Jianhua, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Lixia, Lawyer of Beijing Huamao Silicon Valley Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Tian Ruihua, Lawyer of Beijing Huamao Silicon Valley Law Firm.

The appellant, Bank of China Beijing Branch (hereinafter referred to as BOC Beijing Branch), appeals against the civil judgment (2002) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 839 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over letter of credit advance payment with the respondents Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Lida Oceanarium) and Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as BTI Company), and hereby appeals to this Court. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law, with Presiding Judge Wang Yun, and Acting Judges Gao Shawei and Chen Jizhong as members, and held a public hearing. The appellant's agents ad litem Zhang Huaizhou and Yu Fan, and the respondents' agents ad litem Han Jiayi, Liu Yingzi, Zhang Lixia, and Tian Ruihua appeared in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

Between July and December 1998, Lida Oceanarium submitted 24 "Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit Applications" to BOC Beijing Branch. BTI Company issued an irrevocable payment guarantee for each letter of credit, each guarantee undertaking to ensure that the required funds would be paid from its deposit account (account number: 01619809432014) with BOC Beijing Branch upon receipt of BOC Beijing Branch's payment notice. Each guarantee stated that its validity period was one month after the expiry date of the corresponding letter of credit. BOC Beijing Branch subsequently issued 24 documentary letters of credit to foreign beneficiaries: No. LC1101024/98, for USD 420,000; No. LC1101026/98, for USD 950,000; No. LC1101068/98, for USD 600,672; No. LC1101099/98, for USD 999,716.56; No. LC1101100/98, for USD 650,070; No. LC1101101/98, for USD 756,150; No. LC1101102/98, for USD 619,240; No. LC1101104/98, for USD 804,636.90; No. LC1101105/98, for USD 635,239.66; No. LC1101106/98, for USD 889,335.51; No. LC1101107/98, for USD 931,684.83; No. LC1101116/98, for USD 513,632.70; No. LC1101117/98, for USD 486,637.38; No. LC1101118/98, for USD 642,664.75; No. LC1101119/98, for USD 874,530.64; No. LC1101171/98, for USD 589,700; No. LC1101255/98, for USD 3,518,565; No. LC1101316/98, for USD 808,000; No. LC1101317/98, for USD 992,180; No. LC1101318/98, for USD 2,721,099; No. LC1101319/98, for USD 404,000; No. LC1101320/98, for USD 870,100; No. LC1101321/98, for USD 958,150; No. LC1102128/98, for USD 3,587,840. After the expiry of the letters of credit, BOC Beijing Branch made advance payments totaling USD 24,604,128.49 and RMB 5,266,263.83 for the amounts due under the above letters of credit. Lida Oceanarium failed to repay the said advance payments. On June 22, 2000, BOC Beijing Branch sent to Lida Oceanarium a lawyer's letter demanding repayment of the advance payments under the letters of credit, which was received by Lida Oceanarium on the same day. On August 4, 2000, February 21, 2001, and May 15, 2001, BOC Beijing Branch sent notices to Lida Oceanarium demanding repayment of the advances under the letters of credit, which were received by Lida Oceanarium. On November 23, 2001, BOC Beijing Branch sent a payment reminder to Lida Oceanarium, which was received by Lida Oceanarium. On June 21, 2002, BOC Beijing Branch sent a payment reminder to Lida Oceanarium by mail, which was notarized by the Beijing Notary Public Office. On June 22, 2000, BOC Beijing Branch sent a lawyer's letter to BTI Company, which was received by BTI Company on June 23. The receipt for the lawyer's letter explicitly stated that BTI Company would continue to perform its joint and several guarantee liability. On December 28, 2002, BOC Beijing Branch sent a notice to BTI Company demanding repayment of the advances under the letters of credit, which was received by BTI Company. The receipt for the notice explicitly stated that BTI Company would continue to perform its joint and several guarantee liability. On March 7, 2002, BOC Beijing Branch sent a payment reminder by mail to BTI Company, demanding that BTI Company perform its joint and several guarantee liability and promptly raise funds to repay the principal and interest on the advances owed by Lida Oceanarium to BOC Beijing Branch, and stipulating that the guarantee period would be two years from the date of receipt of this payment reminder. The Beijing Notary Public Office notarized the process of mailing the payment reminder, and the Eastern District Express Delivery Company of the Beijing Postal Administration certified that the payment reminder had been received by BTI Company. BTI Company denied having received the payment reminder dated March 7, 2002.

The court of first instance further found that on February 29, 2000, the Beijing Foreign Exchange Control Department of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange issued an administrative penalty decision (Jing Hui [2000] No. 36) against Lida Oceanarium. The administrative penalty decision stated that Lida Oceanarium, without a genuine trade background, applied to BOC Beijing Branch for the issuance of 68 letters of credit totaling USD 89.34 million between October 1997 and February 1999, of which 39 letters of credit, totaling USD 37.25 million, were discounted by foreign negotiating banks to obtain USD 34.27 million, which was used to pay installation fees, consulting fees, and repay loan interest and principal under non-trade items. The remaining 29 letters of credit, totaling USD 52.09 million, were used for overseas financing by BTI Company. This conduct violated Article 4 of the Measures for the Administration of Borrowing of International Commercial Loans by Domestic Institutions. Pursuant to Article 44 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control, the department decided to impose a fine of RMB 500,000 on Lida Oceanarium. On April 20, 2000, the Beijing Foreign Exchange Control Department of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange issued an administrative penalty decision (Jing Hui Fa [2000] No. 8) against BOC Beijing Branch. The administrative penalty decision stated that between July 1998 and February 1999, BOC Beijing Branch issued 21 letters of credit with a term of 360 days totaling USD 34.71 million for Lida Oceanarium without approval from the foreign exchange authority. This conduct violated Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Risk Management of Commercial Banks' International Settlement Forward Letter of Credit Business. Pursuant to Article 44, Paragraph 4 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control, the department decided to impose a fine of RMB 500,000 on BOC Beijing Branch for the above conduct. BOC Beijing Branch stated that the opening commission, acceptance commission, and cable charges claimed in its lawsuit were charged in accordance with the Bank of China document Zhong Yin Ye (1997) No. 71, "Notice on Issuing the New Charging Rate Table for Foreign Exchange Business of Bank of China."

On March 30, 2000, BTI Company completed a name change registration with the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce, changing its name to Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd., the defendant in this case.

The above facts are supported by evidence including the irrevocable documentary letter of credit applications, irrevocable payment guarantees, documentary letters of credit, lawyer's letters demanding repayment of advances under the letters of credit, notices demanding repayment of advances under the letters of credit, payment reminders, notarized certificates of the Beijing Notary Public Office, certificates of the Eastern District Express Delivery Company of the Beijing Postal Administration, documents of Bank of China, administrative penalty decisions issued by the Beijing Foreign Exchange Control Department of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and court hearing transcripts.

Regarding the above facts found by the court of first instance, apart from BTI Company's denial of having received the payment reminder dated March 7, 2002, and its argument that the guarantee period had expired and the guarantor's liability should be discharged, the parties did not raise any other objections during the second instance, and this Court confirms these facts.

BOC Beijing Branch alleged in its complaint: The bank had made advance payments under the 24 documentary letters of credit issued for Lida Oceanarium. Despite repeated demands, Lida Oceanarium and BTI Company, although having promised to perform the repayment obligation, had failed to repay the above amounts. Therefore, BOC Beijing Branch requested the court to enter judgment: 1. Ordering Lida Oceanarium to repay the principal of the letter of credit advances of USD 24,604,128.49 and RMB 5,266,263.83, and to pay the relevant interest (as of September 20, 2002, USD 6,984,727.94 and RMB 4,326,136.99), and to pay the overdue opening commission of USD 37,808.77, acceptance commission of USD 241,134.69, cable charges of RMB 7,200, and translation fees of RMB 25,055.44. Ordering BTI Company to bear joint and several liability for the above debts; 2. Ordering Lida Oceanarium and BTI Company to bear all litigation costs of this case.

The Beijing High People's Court held: The Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates that commercial banks shall comply with the relevant provisions of laws and administrative regulations when conducting credit business and shall not harm national interests or public interests. BOC Beijing Branch violated Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the Notice of the People's Bank of China on Risk Management of Commercial Banks' International Settlement Forward Letter of Credit Business by issuing multiple 360-day letters of credit for Lida Oceanarium without approval from the foreign exchange authority. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange imposed a penalty on BOC Beijing Branch pursuant to Article 44, Paragraph 4 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control. Lida Oceanarium applied to BOC Beijing Branch for the issuance of letters of credit without a genuine trade background, violating Article 4 of the Measures for the Administration of Borrowing of International Commercial Loans by Domestic Institutions. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange imposed a penalty on Lida Oceanarium pursuant to Article 44 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control. Therefore, the principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit between Lida Oceanarium and BOC Beijing Branch constitutes a financing act carried out with full knowledge that there was no genuine trade background, in violation of national financial management laws and administrative regulations, and shall be held invalid. In this regard, both Lida Oceanarium and BOC Beijing Branch were at fault for the invalidity of the contract and shall bear corresponding liability respectively. The irrevocable payment guarantee issued by BTI Company for the principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit is invalid due to the invalidity of the main contract. Lida Oceanarium used USD 52.09 million from the letters of credit applied for without a genuine trade background for overseas financing by BTI Company. Therefore, it shall be determined that BTI Company was aware of the circumstances under which Lida Oceanarium issued letters of credit without a genuine trade background, and accordingly, BTI Company as the guarantor was also at fault and shall bear corresponding civil compensation liability. BOC Beijing Branch's claim that Lida Oceanarium should compensate it for the actual expenses incurred for opening commission, acceptance commission, cable charges, and translation fees is well founded and shall be upheld. Lida Oceanarium shall compensate BOC Beijing Branch for the losses caused by the letters of credit applied for without a genuine trade background. Lida Oceanarium's defense that the contract in this case is invalid and it should only bear partial liability for the principal, and BTI Company's defense that the main contract is invalid and the guarantee contract is invalid, and therefore it should not bear guarantee liability, are both untenable. Pursuant to Articles 52(1)(3) and (5), 56, and 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 8 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit between Bank of China Beijing Branch and Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. is invalid. The irrevocable payment guarantees issued by Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. for each letter of credit are invalid; 2. Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. shall repay the principal of the letter of credit advances of USD 24,604,128.49 and RMB 5,266,263.83 to Bank of China Beijing Branch, and compensate for corresponding losses (the losses shall be calculated from the date of each advance payment, with both USD and RMB calculated according to the current demand deposit interest rate stipulated by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period); 3. Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. shall repay to Bank of China Beijing Branch the opening commission of USD 37,808.77, acceptance commission of USD 241,134.69, cable charges of RMB 7,200, and translation fees of RMB 25,055.44; 4. Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. shall bear compensation liability for one-third of the amount that cannot be recovered from the payments to Bank of China Beijing Branch by Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. under items 2 and 3 above; 5. The other claims of Bank of China Beijing Branch are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,372,527.18 shall be borne jointly by Beijing Lida Oceanarium Co., Ltd. and Beijing International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 1,000,000 (to be paid to this court within seven days after this judgment takes effect); and by Bank of China Beijing Branch in the amount of RMB 372,527.18.

BOC Beijing Branch, dissatisfied with the above judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing: I. This case is a dispute over letter of credit advance payment, which is a type of letter of credit dispute and should be governed by the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (hereinafter referred to as UCP500). (A) The parties explicitly chose to apply UCP500. Pursuant to Article 1 of UCP500, UCP500 is binding on all parties concerned. (B) Pursuant to Article 2 of UCP500, the issuing bank and the applicant are parties to the letter of credit and should be bound by UCP500. (C) Based on the definition of a letter of credit and Article 18 of UCP500, disputes over letter of credit advance payment fall within the scope of UCP500. II. The first instance judgment erroneously treated the letter of credit advance payment dispute as a so-called "principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit" dispute, departing from the nature of letters of credit. (A) The principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit is actually the application for a letter of credit, which is not an independent legal act but is subsumed within the legal relationship of letters of credit. There was never any principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit between the bank and the oceanarium; there was only the oceanarium's application for a letter of credit. From a contractual perspective, an application for a letter of credit is a unilateral act constituting an offer, and the contractual relationship between the parties does not arise until the bank issues the letter of credit. (B) A dispute over letter of credit advance payment is a letter of credit dispute, not a dispute over a principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit. According to the definition of a letter of credit, a letter of credit governs two types of relationships: 1. The relationship between the issuing bank and other banks and the beneficiary, from which disputes over letter of credit payment arise; 2. The relationship between the applicant and the issuing bank, from which disputes over letter of credit advance payment arise. (C) According to the result of the first instance judgment, the principal-agent contract for the issuance of letters of credit is invalid, and the consequence of an invalid legal act is that it is void ab initio. The letter of credit issued would naturally also be invalid, entitling the bank to refuse payment, which clearly contradicts UCP500. III. The first instance judgment erroneously determined the main contract for the "Guarantee." The main contract for the "Guarantee" in this case is the letter of credit. The letter of credit is valid, and the "Guarantee" is also valid. Therefore, BTI Company should bear guarantee liability. From the name and content of the "Irrevocable Payment Guarantee" issued by BTI Company, a clear conclusion can be drawn: this guarantee was issued against the applicant's payment obligation under the letter of credit. As soon as the applicant's payment obligation to the issuing bank arises, the guarantee liability arises accordingly. Therefore, where the letter of credit is valid and an advance has been made, BTI Company should naturally bear guarantee liability. IV. The first instance judgment erroneously handled the interest. According to the result of the first instance judgment, the liability of the applicant who maliciously opened letters of credit without a trade background is actually lighter than that under a normal letter of credit advance, thereby facilitating the use of letters of credit by unscrupulous individuals for financing. In this case, the bank is the only party that suffered losses, while Lida Oceanarium and BTI Company are the wrongdoers. However, according to the result of the first instance judgment, the liability of Lida Oceanarium and BTI Company is lighter than that under a normal letter of credit advance, which is manifestly unfair. According to the letter of credit issuance procedure, the bank cannot verify the authenticity of the trade background when issuing a letter of credit. Some applicants precisely use this characteristic of letters of credit for financing. If the result of the first instance judgment is followed, the liability for issuing letters of credit without a genuine trade background for financing would be lighter than the liability for normal letter of credit advances, which will inevitably open the door wide for unscrupulous individuals, increase bank losses, and make it difficult for banks to conduct letter of credit business in the future. This would have a tremendous impact on the entire financial order. In summary, this case is a letter of credit dispute and should be governed by UCP500. Lida Oceanarium should be ordered to bear the responsibility of repaying the advance payments, and BTI Company provided an effective guarantee for the payment obligation under the letter of credit and should bear guarantee liability. The result of the first instance judgment indulged the wrongdoers and increased the losses of the innocent party, and should be corrected.

北国投公司答辩称：一、中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间的委托开证合同系没有真实贸易背景并违反国家金融管理法律和行政法规的无效法律行为，北京市高级人民法院的认定定性准确，适用法律正确。（一）中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间订立的委托开证合同实际上是以委托开证为名，行违法融资之实，本案涉及的信用证全部属于无真实贸易背景的信用证。（二）中行北京分行与利达海洋馆非法融资开立无真实贸易背景信用证的行为违反了我国强制性法律规定。（三）中行北京分行与利达海洋馆开具无真实贸易背景信用证的行为已经受到国家外汇管理局北京外汇管理部的行政处罚。二、由于委托开证合同无效，本案担保合同依法亦应当无效，且担保人不应再承担任何担保责任。三、本案信用证最后一笔截止日期是1999年10月31日，根据约定，本案保函的有效保证期最迟到1999年11月31日，而中行北京分行第一次向北国投公司主张承担保证责任的时间是2000年6月22日，超过了保函规定的保证责任期限。根据担保法第二十六条的规定，保证合同的保证期限已过，北国投公司的保证责任应当免除。因此，请求依法驳回上诉，维护答辩人的合法权益。

利达海洋馆没有提交书面答辩状。开庭时明确表示，原审判决认定事实正确，适用法律亦正确。

本院认为，本案系因中行北京分行为利达海洋馆开立信用证并支付信用证款项后，利达海洋馆及其担保人北国投公司未能偿还中行北京分行对外支付的信用证项下的款项，而形成的信用证垫付款及担保纠纷案。经审理查明，利达海洋馆申请开立信用证的真实意思并非为了进口货物，而是为了融资，套取国家外汇。根据法律规定，当事人的民事法律行为应当意思表示真实。本案中，中行北京分行与利达海洋馆签订合同的意思表示并不真实一致，其结果是以合法形式掩盖非法目的，并导致银行大笔资金外流，损害国家利益。故原审关于中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间委托开证合同无效的认定正确，本院予以维持。

本案中行北京分行根据利达海洋馆的开证申请对外开出信用证，虽然中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间没有达成一项明确的开证协议，但双方之间存在委托开立信用证申请书。而开证申请书明确约定了信用证申请人利达海洋馆与开证行中行北京分行的权利义务，成为规范利达海洋馆与中行北京分行法律行为的基础法律文件。当利达海洋馆没有按照开证申请书的约定偿付信用证项下的款项时，中行北京分行便依据开证申请书，请求利达海洋馆付款。因此，从开证申请书的内容和开证行的行为可以认定在中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间已经形成委托开证法律关系。根据信用证独立原则，信用证一经开出，委托开证法律关系即与信用证相互独立，开证申请人不能以信用证以外的理由要求开证行撤回已开立的信用证，银行在处理信用证业务时也不受委托开证合同的约束。本案中行北京分行无视其与利达海洋馆之间已经存在的委托开证法律关系，将委托开证法律关系与信用证本身相混淆，该行关于中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间不存在委托开证合同，委托开证合同不是一个独立的法律行为，本案属于信用证纠纷，不是委托开证合同纠纷的上诉理由不能成立，本院不予支持。

本案当事人明确选择适用UCP500，从UCP500第一、二条以及第三条的规定可以看出，该惯例的适用排除了开证行与开证申请人之间的委托开证法律关系，开证行与开证申请人之间的委托开证关系不受其调整，本案中行北京分行与利达海洋馆之间的申请开证法律关系应当适用国内法的有关规定。因此，中行北京分行关于本案应适用UCP500的上诉理由亦不能成立。原审法院适用合同法的规定处理本案正确，本院予以维持。

本案北国投公司根据信用证开证申请人利达海洋馆的要求，出具的不可撤销的付款保函，其担保的是利达海洋馆的付款责任，对于担保合同而言，主合同是利达海洋馆与中行北京分行之间的开证法律关系。中行北京分行关于《保函》的主合同是信用证本身的理由，没有事实和法律依据，本院不予支持。原审判决认定北国投公司为委托开证出具的不可撤销付款保函因主合同无效而导致无效，是正确的，本院予以维持。

从本案一、二审事实看，中行北京分行开证时间过于集中，即在短期内，连续为利达海洋馆开出几十份信用证，本案涉及24份，且数额巨大。按照银行的规定，开立信用证超过100万美元的，必须经过中国银行总行批准，中行北京分行为了规避这一规定，使信用证顺利开出，将每笔信用证控制在100万美元以下。就本案事实可以认定中行北京分行应当知道利达海洋馆所开立的信用证并不具有真实的基础交易背景，据此，中行北京分行在本案中是具有过错的，应当承担相应的过错责任。中行北京分行关于一审判决结果显失公平的主张，没有事实和法律依据，本院不予支持。

本案担保人北国投公司关于保证合同的保证期限已过，保证人保证责任应予免除的主张，由于北国投公司没有提出上诉，故本院不予考虑。原审判决认定北国投公司作为担保人，在本案中亦具有过错，应当承担相应的民事责任，是正确的，应予维持。

综上，原审判决认定事实清楚，判决结果正确，应予维持。依据《中华人民共和国民事诉讼法》第一百五十三条第一款第（一）项之规定，判决如下：

驳回上诉，维持原判。

一审案件受理费按照一审判决承担；二审案件受理费人民币1372527.18元，由上诉人中国银行北京市分行承担。

本判决为终审判决。

审判长  王   玧

代理审判员  高莎薇

代理审判员  陈纪忠

二〇〇四年二月二日

书记员  付晓强（代）

王玧高级法官：1955年出生，法学硕士。2003年起任最高人民法院民事审判第四庭副庭长。
